name: Root-Critical Wedges Are Corner-Peelable
statement: Every root-critical pointed cover-recursively peripheral partial cube has a corner peeling ending at its root. Therefore every one-vertex-decomposable forbidden pc-minor for the cover-recursively peripheral class is corner-peelable.
proof: First induct through a root-avoiding decomposition to build an isometric-prefix order beginning at the root: order the contraction-base layer first and append an isometric-prefix order of the duplicated site. For a root-critical pair, a peripheral coordinate has both its root-side restriction and contraction root-avoidable; interleave their root-first orders across the two layers to obtain an isometric-prefix order of the whole factor. For a wedge, list the common root, then one factor, then the other; distances between factors add through the root. Reversing these orders gives the required peelings.
